title: aSAH numbers
scopeNote: Rounds lookup, not a protocol. Glucose and temperature (Hoh §8 Recs 7–8) intentionally omitted. Hb thresholds: see Neuro-ICU targets card.

rows.target: No specific SBP target — frequent BP monitoring, short-acting agents; avoid severe hypotension, hypertension and BP variability
notes: Severe hypertension (>180–200 mm Hg): lower gradually; avoid MAP <65 (writing-group text)
Earlier guidelines used SBP <160 or <180 — may be reasonable, evidence insufficient for a target
Meta-analysis: more rebleeding with SBP >160, not with <140
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436

rows.target: Emergency reversal
notes: Follow current standards for life-threatening bleeding
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436

rows.target: Not useful to improve functional outcome
notes: ULTRA: ultra-early TXA didn't improve 6-month outcome
evidenceNote: Hoh 2023 §6 Rec 3: COR 3: No Benefit, LOE A
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436

rows.target: 60 mg enteral q4h × 21 days; start as soon as possible, within 96 h of onset
notes: Keep giving through hypotension that standard measures can manage; hold temporarily only for significant BP variability (Hoh text)
Cirrhosis: 30 mg q4h with close BP/HR monitoring (label)
1 h before or 2 h after meals; avoid grapefruit (label)
Can't swallow: puncture both capsule ends with an 18 G needle, draw contents into an oral/enteral syringe labeled 'Not for IV Use', give via NG/PEG, flush with 30 mL NS (label)
Never IV or other parenteral route — boxed warning (label)
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors contraindicated; strong inducers (phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, rifampin) generally not co-administered (label)
IV and intra-arterial nimodipine: too little data to recommend (Hoh)
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436
Nimodipine capsules US prescribing information. Bionpharma Inc.; revised 12/2025 (DailyMed label)

notes: Peak DCI/vasospasm risk: post-bleed days 6–10 (Hoh §8.3 text)
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436

rows.target: Euvolemia — close monitoring and goal-directed treatment
notes: CVP alone isn't an adequate measure of volume status
Definitions of euvolemia vary; no clear standard
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436

rows.target: Potentially harmful — excess morbidity
notes: RCTs: more complications without less DCI or better outcome
evidenceNote: Hoh 2023 §8 Rec 5: COR 3: Harm, LOE B-R
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436

rows.target: No prophylactic hemodynamic augmentation
notes: No outcome benefit; more complications including heart failure (Hoh text)
evidenceNote: Hoh 2023 §8.3 Rec 8: COR 3: Harm, LOE B-R
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436

rows.target: Mineralocorticoid (fludrocortisone) is reasonable
notes: RCTs: less natriuresis, urine volume, hyponatremia and IV fluid use; DCI and outcome not consistently improved
Main adverse effect: hypokalemia — potassium supplementation
High-dose hydrocortisone: similar sodium effects, more complications (hyperglycemia, hypokalemia, GI bleeding, heart failure)
No dose in the provided sources — use pharmacy dosing
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436

rows.target: Raising SBP may be reasonable to limit DCI
notes: Hoh Figure 3 labels its DCI-response box (elevate BP, ensure euvolemia, imaging) Class 2a; the recommendation table says 2b — table used
Retrospective: more neurological improvement with norepinephrine than phenylephrine (94% vs 71%)
HIMALAIA (only RCT) stopped early, underpowered
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436

rows.target: Pharmacological or mechanical prophylaxis
notes: Small RCT: enoxaparin 40 mg SC daily after aneurysm treatment didn't increase bleeding
Optimal timing relative to securing and procedures is unclear (Hoh text)
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436

pitfalls: Don't stop nimodipine for manageable hypotension — interruptions were associated with more DCI (Hoh text)
Nimodipine plus phenytoin: phenytoin is both a strong CYP3A4 inducer (label) and harmful as SAH prophylaxis (Hoh)
keyNumbers: Nimodipine 60 mg q4h × 21 d (30 mg q4h in cirrhosis)
Unsecured: no SBP target; avoid MAP <65 and BP swings
Euvolemia; no prophylactic hypervolemia or augmentation
Seizure ppx only if high-risk; no phenytoin; ASM ≤7 d
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436
